subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should `models status --probe --all` become the canonical configured-model health check, or should this behavior be folded into fallback-chain testing or staged model migration UX?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this adds a new live CLI probe mode that makes real provider requests and overlaps two adjacent model-diagnostics feature requests.

options.title: Approve Scoped Status Probe
options.body: Add `--probe --all` as the broad configured-model health sweep while keeping fallback-chain and staged-migration work separate.

options.title: Fold Into Fallback Testing
options.body: Make the targeted fallback-chain command own configured fallback validation and avoid a second broad probe surface for now.

options.title: Defer To Migration UX
options.body: Treat per-model probing as one step in a staged model migration workflow and leave this issue open until that larger UX is scoped.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped Status Probe
recommendation.body: Add `--probe --all` as the broad configured-model health sweep while keeping fallback-chain and staged-migration work separate.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined history across model status/probe, auth-health, and provider routing surfaces in the evidence set.
